23 The diagram shows the screen of a cathode-ray oscilloscope (c.r.o.) displaying a wave.
The time-base of the c.r.o. is set at 10 ms / division.
What is the frequency of the wave?
A
0.24 Hz
B
4.2 Hz
C
12 Hz
D
24 Hz

hints: Count the horizontal divisions for one full sine cycle on the c.r.o. screen, from a rising zero-crossing to the next rising zero-crossing.
Multiply that number of divisions by the time-base of $10 \text{ ms}$ per division to get the period $T$ in $\text{ms}$, then convert to seconds.
Use $f = 1/T$ with $T$ in seconds and check that a period near $40 \text{ ms}$ gives a frequency of tens of hertz.
walkthrough: Look along the time axis and isolate one complete oscillation, for example from one upward crossing of the central line to the next identical upward crossing.
Measure its horizontal length. It spans about 4.2 divisions on the screen grid.
Calculate frequency from $f = 1/T$: $f \approx 1/0.042 \text{ s} \approx 23.8 \text{ Hz}$, about $24 \text{ Hz}$ with sensible precision.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100. It treats the 42 ms period as 4.2 s by omitting the milli- to SI conversion.

B.explanation: Too small by about a factor of 6. It does not follow from $T \approx 42 \text{ ms}$ and $f = 1/T$.

C.explanation: Half the correct frequency. It doubles the period to about 8.4 divisions, which is two cycles counted as one.
